title: Trump's January 2025 Order Directs Restrictions on Care for Minors and Federal Custody Inquiries
description_short: Trump's Jan. 28 order directed limits on federal support for gender-transition care for minors and DOJ action on state custody practices affecting supportive parents.
description_medium: On Jan. 28, 2025, Trump signed EO 14187, directing federal agencies to stop specified forms of federal support for gender-transition procedures for minors and to take related steps through grants, health programs, insurance, and TRICARE. It also directs DOJ to investigate providers and address state custody practices involving supportive parents. This documents an executive directive, not completed prosecutions of parents or actual custody removals.
description_long: On January 28, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14187. The order directs federal agencies to stop specified forms of federal support for gender-transition procedures for minors and calls for related steps through grants, health programs, insurance, and TRICARE. It also directs the Department of Justice to investigate providers and address state custody practices involving supportive parents. These provisions describe federal policy and instructions to agencies. The available account does not establish that supportive parents were prosecuted, that criminal penalties were imposed on them, or that custody was actually removed. Those distinctions keep the entry focused on what the order directs: changes in federal support and DOJ attention to provider and custody matters. They do not establish that each directed step was carried out or that a particular family experienced enforcement. The event is the signed executive directive itself, with implementation outcomes left unspecified by the available record.
